Hi Karthik,

We're in the final leg of procurement and Acme's legal team asked for a short, plain-language explanation of a few items for our risk committee: a) who your subprocessors are at a high level (no need for confidential vendor contracts), b) what countries data might be transferred to when using the hosted API, and c) a 2–3 sentence explanation we can put in our procurement summary about how Redwood protects customer data in transit and at rest.

They'd prefer something that the non-technical reviewers can read in under two minutes. Can you or someone from your team send a one-pager or a short blurb we can paste into our memo?

Appreciate it — we need this by EOD Wednesday if possible.

Thanks,

Thanks Karthik — I reviewed the draft and made targeted edits. Main points:

- Keep the procurement memo paragraph concise (recommended ~3 sentences). Removed technical jargon such as "KV cache" and "quantization" — not relevant for Acme's risk committee.
- For subprocessors: provide categories (cloud infra, logging/monitoring, analytics) and a link to the live subprocessor map rather than naming every vendor in the one-pager. This keeps the memo readable and complies with our vendor disclosure practice.
- For transfers: be explicit that customer data may traverse or be processed in the US and EU; include statement about standard contractual clauses and how customers can request data locality references in Dedicated/Private options.
- Suggested FAQ entries for the Console DPA notice (2–3 bullets) — simple Q/A about retention, deletion requests, and evidence of SOC2.

I attached the edited summary (DPA-exec-summary-v2.docx) and the CSV map we use for legal processes (redwood-subprocessor-map.csv).

I also recommend we avoid the phrase "onshore-only" — ambiguous and could introduce procurement questions. Instead: "We route requests to regionally appropriate infrastructure and offer special deployment options for customers with residency requirements."

If Acme wants an evidence package (SOC 2 report + subprocessors), we can share a redacted bundle after NDA.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference
